name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known specifically as the son of Shephatiah. His identity is primarily grounded in this familial connection, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8. There are no additional notes or distinguishing details provided about his life or role in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam is a proper name meaning 'restitution.' This meaning is noted but not explicitly tied to any divine naming or special title. It simply identifies him as Meshullam within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Meshullam as the son of Shephatiah. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text for Meshullam.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance in the biblical narrative is connected to his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin. Through his identification as the son of Shephatiah, he contributes to the preservation of the lineage important for understanding the heritage of God's people. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:8 serves to affirm the continuity of the Benjaminite family lines during the post-exilic period.
